sources.citation: Wang X, Li A, Wang W, Que H, Zhang G, Li L (2021). DNA methylation mediates differentiation in thermal responses of Pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas) derived from different tidal levels. Heredity 126:10-22.
sources.read: full text (PMC7852555 HTML, incl. Table 1 and figure legends) and both supplements (ESM1 .doc: Figs S1-S7 legends only, figure images not inspected; ESM2 .pdf: Tables S1-S4 in full)

claims.statement: Intertidal control oysters (InC) had a mean CpG methylation level of 15.0%.
claims.re_derived: 12.74% (mean over 3 samples, origin = In, temperature = C; CpG calls pooled per library); paper 15.0%

claims.statement: Subtidal control oysters (SubC) had a mean CpG methylation level of 14.5%.
claims.re_derived: 12.37% (mean over 3 samples, origin = Sub, temperature = C; CpG calls pooled per library); paper 14.5%

claims.statement: Heat-shocked intertidal oysters (InH) had a mean CpG methylation level of 13.4%.
claims.re_derived: 11.50% (mean over 3 samples, origin = In, temperature = H; CpG calls pooled per library); paper 13.4%

claims.statement: Heat-shocked subtidal oysters (SubH) had a mean CpG methylation level of 15.4%.
claims.re_derived: 13.10% (mean over 3 samples, origin = Sub, temperature = H; CpG calls pooled per library); paper 15.4%

claims.where: Results, Global methylation pattern; Fig. 1a; Discussion para 2
claims.statement: In intertidal oysters, heat shock significantly lowered global CpG methylation (InC 15.0% vs InH 13.4%, ANOVA P < 0.05, n = 3 pools each).
claims.re_derived: temperature C 12.74% vs H 11.50% (difference +1.24 points, n = 3 vs 3, permutation p = 0.0984, the smallest possible with these group sizes is 0.1, groups completely separated, within origin = In)
claims.rule: same direction and p < 0.05 (or, when group sizes cannot reach 0.05, complete separation): replicated; same direction: partly; opposite: not replicated

claims.where: Results, Global methylation pattern; Fig. 1a; Discussion para 2
claims.statement: In subtidal oysters, heat shock slightly raised global CpG methylation (SubC 14.5% vs SubH 15.4%); the paper calls this slight and gives no significance.
claims.re_derived: temperature H 13.10% vs C 12.37% (difference +0.73 points, n = 3 vs 3, permutation p = 0.0984, the smallest possible with these group sizes is 0.1, groups completely separated, within origin = Sub)
claims.rule: same direction and p < 0.05 (or, when group sizes cannot reach 0.05, complete separation): replicated; same direction: partly; opposite: not replicated

claims.statement: Under control conditions intertidal oysters were marginally more methylated than subtidal oysters (15.0% vs 14.5%); no test of this difference is reported in the text.
claims.re_derived: origin In 12.74% vs Sub 12.37% (difference +0.37 points, n = 3 vs 3, permutation p = 0.401, the smallest possible with these group sizes is 0.1, within temperature = C)
claims.rule: same direction and p < 0.05 (or, when group sizes cannot reach 0.05, complete separation): replicated; same direction: partly; opposite: not replicated

claims.statement: Non-CpG methylation was very low in control oysters: 0.20% of CHG and 0.16% of CHH sites methylated on average.
claims.re_derived: Values are split by CHG and CHH context; our pipeline reports non-CpG methylation pooled per library, which can be compared only loosely (expect well under 1%). Our values are also uncorrected for conversion while the paper's are lambda-corrected.

claims.statement: Hierarchical clustering of the 12 methylomes grouped samples by tidal origin rather than by heat treatment (except two SubH samples that branched apart).
claims.re_derived: only a PCA's PC1 and PC2 are kept, not hierarchical clustering

claims.statement: In PCA of the 12 samples, PC1 separated intertidal from subtidal oysters.
claims.re_derived: origin explains 82% (adjusted R^2) of PC1 (20.98% of variance); PCA of job main

claims.statement: PC2 separated heat-shocked from control samples, with the heat effect pointing in opposite directions for intertidal and subtidal oysters.
claims.re_derived: temperature explains 0% (adjusted R^2) of PC2 (12.81% of variance); PCA of job main

claims.where: Results, Global methylation pattern; Fig. 1d; Discussion para 3
claims.statement: DAPC showed a larger heat-induced methylation shift (greater plasticity) in intertidal than subtidal oysters (MCMC P < 0.05), with intertidal shifting down and subtidal up.
claims.re_derived: DAPC on gene methylation at common C sites with an MCMC mixed model of shift length; no comparable analysis in our outputs. The direction part overlaps C5/C6 and the per-gene direction claims C17/C19; an origin x temperature interaction is not a registered contrast.

claims.where: Results, Correlation between DNA methylation status and gene expression; Fig. 3b; Discussion para 2
claims.statement: Methylation is concentrated in gene bodies, with other genomic regions less methylated.
claims.re_derived: gene_body 17.30% vs genome 12.43% (CpG calls pooled over all genes, mean over samples)

claims.statement: Gene-body methylation correlated positively with gene expression in all four groups; non-expressed genes had the lowest methylation and high/medium-expression genes the highest.
claims.re_derived: Uses matched RNA-seq (PRJNA407831) FPKM; no r value given in the text.

claims.where: Results, Estimation of genotypic effect; Fig. 2
claims.statement: Libraries clustered genetically by tidal origin (SNPs from WGBS reads), but per-gene FST between InC and SubC was barely correlated with methylation difference (r = 0.02 gene body, 0.01 exon; 16,516 genes), so methylation divergence was argued to be largely independent of genotype.
claims.re_derived: Requires SNP calling and FST per gene; not in our outputs.

claims.where: Results, DNA methylation differentiation ... in response to heat stress; Fig. 6a
claims.statement: Heat shock in intertidal oysters gave 2137 DMGs (491 hyper, 1646 hypo in InH vs InC). The paper's Venn counts (788 shared + 1279 intertidal-unique = 2067) do not add up to this total.
claims.re_derived: job main, temperatureH: gene_body: 53 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 0.906); promoter: 40 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 0.865); paper 2137 DMGs
claims.rule: genes vs genes: within 3x of the paper's count replicated; fewer or more but some: partly; none: not replicated; approximate: our job pools over origin (paper: In only), so at most partly

claims.statement: Most heat-responsive DMGs in intertidal oysters were hypomethylated (1646 of 2137, 77%).
claims.re_derived: job main, temperatureH: 35 higher and 58 lower in H (FDR < 0.05, both regions)
claims.rule: majority direction of >= 5 significant genes; approximate: our job pools over origin (paper: In only), so at most partly

claims.statement: Heat shock in subtidal oysters gave 2459 DMGs (1636 hyper, 823 hypo in SubH vs SubC). The paper's Venn counts (788 shared + 1554 subtidal-unique = 2342) do not add up to this total.
claims.re_derived: job main, temperatureH: gene_body: 53 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 0.906); promoter: 40 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 0.865); paper 2459 DMGs
claims.rule: genes vs genes: within 3x of the paper's count replicated; fewer or more but some: partly; none: not replicated; approximate: our job pools over origin (paper: Sub only), so at most partly

claims.statement: Most heat-responsive DMGs in subtidal oysters were hypermethylated (1636 of 2459, 66.5%), opposite to intertidal oysters.
claims.re_derived: job main, temperatureH: 35 higher and 58 lower in H (FDR < 0.05, both regions)
claims.rule: majority direction of >= 5 significant genes; approximate: our job pools over origin (paper: Sub only), so at most partly

claims.where: Results, DNA methylation differentiation ... under temperate conditions; Fig. 4a; Fig. S3
claims.statement: Intertidal and subtidal control oysters differed in methylation at many genes (InC vs SubC DMGs, all C contexts), but the total number of DMGs is not reported, only the 90 that were also DEGs.
claims.re_derived: job main, originIn: gene_body: 1622 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 1.669); promoter: 540 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 1.13)
claims.rule: genes vs genes: within 3x of the paper's count replicated; fewer or more but some: partly; none: not replicated; approximate: our job pools over temperature (paper: C only), so at most partly; test statistics are inflated (lambda 1.669 > 1.3), so the count is not trusted: at most partly

claims.statement: The opposite heat responses (InH below InC, SubH above SubC) held across promoter, exon, intron and repeat regions and in DMRs, and a heatmap of all DMRs clustered samples by tidal origin.
claims.re_derived: Exon, intron, repeat and DMR-level summaries are not available; the promoter part is only indirectly reflected in the per-gene promoter direction counts of C17/C19.

claims.where: Results; Fig. 6b-d, Fig. S6, Table S3

claims.where: Results; Fig. 4a, Fig. 6b; Abstract; Discussion para 5
claims.statement: DMGs overlapped DEGs: 90 genes (11.46% of DEGs) for InC vs SubC, 67 (10.65%) for InH vs InC and 55 (6.88%) for SubH vs SubC; among the intertidal overlap genes 77% were hypomethylated, and 62% of subtidal overlap genes were hypermethylated with higher expression.
claims.re_derived: Overlap with RNA-seq DEGs from PRJNA407831.

claims.where: Results; Fig. 4c, Fig. 6b, Figs S3-S4; Abstract
claims.statement: Heat-responsive methylation-regulated genes were enriched for apoptosis and development in intertidal oysters and for oxidation-reduction and ion homeostasis in subtidal oysters; origin-differing genes were enriched for cell adhesion, carbohydrate transport and apoptosis.
claims.re_derived: GO/KEGG enrichment on DMG-DEG overlap sets (GOseq, KOBAS); depends on RNA-seq and on the paper's annotation.

claims.statement: Bisulfite PCR of 8 CpGs in HSPA12A (scaffold1801:18940-19215) confirmed WGBS: InC nearly unmethylated, InH higher; SubH higher than SubC.
claims.re_derived: Single-locus CpG validation on the oyster_v9 genome; per-CpG calls and these coordinates are not available.
